mainTopic: The finger lottery and the ban on counting Jews, then aggadah about the sins and kingship of שאול and דוד
overview: The amud opens by ending רב פפא's question about measuring the race up the כבש as תיקו, with no answer. It then explains the משנה's finger lottery (הצביעו): the ממונה counts fingers, not the כהנים themselves, because רבי יצחק teaches that counting Jews directly is forbidden even for a מצוה. After רב אשי questions the verse about בזק, the גמרא proves the rule from שאול counting the people with sheep (טלאים). רבי אלעזר and רב נחמן בר יצחק say counting Jews violates one or two לאוין, and the גמרא resolves an apparent contradiction in the verse in הושע in two ways. The verses about שאול lead to a long aggadic discussion: a leader becomes wealthy, שאול argued against ה׳'s command to destroy עמלק, and a בת קול rebuked him twice. רב הונא contrasts שאול, who lost the kingdom over one sin, with דוד, who kept it despite two, and the גמרא works out which of דוד's sins count. The amud ends with teachings on שאול's innocence, why his dynasty ended, and his punishment for giving up a king's honor. It then begins a teaching about every תלמיד חכם that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second side of רב פפא's measuring question
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא finishes his question: maybe the measurement excludes the cubit of the יסוד and the cubit of the סובב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps the measurement leaves out the cubit of the base and the cubit of the ledge?
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב פפא's question on the previous amud. He offered one way to measure the distance to the מזבח, and now he offers the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The race up the כבש is decided by distance to the מזבח. The question is where the מזבח 'starts.' One option is the spot where the ramp touches the מזבח. The other option leaves out the two cubits of the יסוד and סובב that stick out underneath, which moves the line two cubits farther down the ramp.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)
The cubit of the base of the altar
The cubit of the ledge around the altar

phrases.english: Or perhaps excluding the cubit of the base
phrases.notes: The second possibility in רב פפא's question.

phrases.english: and the cubit of the ledge?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a question begun on the previous amud.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the measurement on the כבש taken including or excluding the cubits of the יסוד and the סובב?

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes תיקו. רב פפא's question has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רב פפא's question without answering it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source was found to decide between the two measurements. The question is left open, and the גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand (the question remains unresolved)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's question about measuring the race to the מזבח (with or without the יסוד and סובב cubits) ends in תיקו. It is never resolved.

phrases.english: Let it stand [unresolved].
phrases.notes: Standard closing for an unanswered question.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question raised in step 1.

steps.title: The משנה: when the race is a tie, the appointed priest says 'extend fingers'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. If two כהנים tied in the race, the ממונה tells everyone to put out their fingers.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the two of them were equal, the appointed one says to them: 'Extend [your fingers],' etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes the next line it wants to discuss. This sets up the explanation of the strange word הצביעו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the first כהן to get close to the מזבח wins the right to clear the ashes. If two arrive at the same moment, there is no winner, so the ממונה switches to a lottery done with fingers.

keyTerms.meaning: The appointed officer in charge of the כהנים
Etc. (the quote continues in the משנה)

phrases.english: And if the two of them were equal,
the appointed one says to them:
'Extend [your fingers],' etc.
phrases.notes: This is the word the גמרא is about to explain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When there is a tie, the ממונה conducts a lottery by having the כהנים extend their fingers.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains the word הצביעו
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains הצביעו: put out your fingers to be counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'Put out your fingers for a count.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא explains the unusual word in the משנה. The lottery works by counting fingers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ממונה picks a number, and each כהן puts out a finger. He then counts around the fingers, and the one where the number lands wins. This explanation leads straight into the next question: why fingers and not people?

phrases.english: It was taught: 'Put out your fingers for a count.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word הצביעו from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הצביעו means to put out fingers so that they can be counted.

steps.title: Why not count the priests themselves?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ממונה counts fingers instead of simply counting the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him count them themselves!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the lottery uses fingers at all, when the ממונה could just count the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting heads would give the same result more simply, so the use of fingers seems unnecessary. The גמרא wants to know the reason behind this indirect method.

phrases.english: But let him count them themselves!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the method described in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is the count done on fingers rather than directly on the כהנים?

steps.title: This supports רבי יצחק
steps.stepSummary: The answer: this practice supports the view of רבי יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבי יצחק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the finger-counting is a support for רבי יצחק. It is about to quote what he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Counting fingers instead of people only makes sense if there is a problem with counting people directly. So the משנה backs up a teaching of רבי יצחק, which the גמרא quotes in the next step.

phrases.english: This supports Rabbi Yitzchak.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Fingers are counted because counting people directly is forbidden, as רבי יצחק teaches.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: it is forbidden to count Jews, even for a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק rules that counting Jews directly is forbidden even for a מצוה. He learns this from שאול counting the people with בזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק said: It is forbidden to count ישראל, even for a מצוה, as it is written: 'And he counted them with בזק.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יצחק's rule and his verse. שאול counted the people indirectly, through בזק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק reads בזק as broken pieces. Each soldier gave a piece, and שאול counted the pieces, not the men. The words 'even for a מצוה' show the rule holds even here in the בית המקדש lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of a מצוה
Here read as shards or broken pieces

steps.confusionAlert: The איסור is counting the people themselves. Counting objects that stand for them (fingers, shards, sheep) is allowed. That is the whole point of the finger lottery.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak said:
It is forbidden to count Israel
even for a מצוה,
as it is written: 'And he counted them with bezek' (I Samuel 11:8).
phrases.notes: Here בזק is read as pieces of broken pottery, one for each man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the teaching that the משנה supports.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to count Jews directly, even for a מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the well-known practice of counting people indirectly (for example, for a מנין) instead of counting heads.

steps.title: רב אשי: maybe בזק is just the name of a town
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges the verse. בזק may be a place name, so the verse could mean שאול counted the people in the town of בזק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: From where do you know that this 'בזק' means breaking? Perhaps it is the name of a town, as it is written: 'And they found אדוני בזק.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the source for רבי יצחק's rule. He does not attack the rule itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בזק is a town, the verse says nothing about how שאול counted. The proof disappears. רב אשי supports this reading from the verse about אדוני בזק, which shows that בזק was a real place.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objected to this:
From where [do you know] that this 'bezek'
is a term meaning 'breaking apart'?
Perhaps it is the name of a town,
as it is written: 'And they found Adoni-bezek' (Judges 1:5).
phrases.notes: Shows that בזק was a place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the verse used in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's reading of בזק as shards.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בזק can be read as a place name, so the verse does not prove that the counting was indirect.

steps.title: A better source: שאול counted them with sheep
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא replaces the verse. שאול counted the people בטלאים, with sheep, which clearly shows indirect counting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, [learn it] from here: 'And שאול summoned the people and counted them with sheep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's challenge and brings a different verse to support the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads טלאים as 'sheep': each soldier set aside a sheep, and the sheep were counted, not the men. The rule of רבי יצחק stays the same; only its source has been changed.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
'And Saul summoned the people
and counted them with sheep' (I Samuel 15:4).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי by switching to a new verse.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule was learned from בזק, read as shards.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is learned from טלאים, which clearly shows that people were counted indirectly.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: counting Jews violates a negative commandment
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that anyone who counts Jews transgresses a לאו. He learns this from the verse 'which cannot be measured.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Whoever counts Israel transgresses a negative commandment, as it is said: 'And the number of the children of Israel will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement explains how serious counting Jews is. It counts as violating a לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'לא ימד' (it cannot be measured) as a command: it may not be measured. So the verse is turned into a prohibition against counting.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the sand of the sea
It shall not (or cannot) be measured

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Whoever counts Israel
transgresses a negative commandment,
as it is said: 'And the number of the children of Israel will be
like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured' (Hosea 2:1).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds how serious the איסור of counting is.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: two negative commandments
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that one who counts Jews violates two לאוין, from 'לא ימד' and 'ולא יספר.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He transgresses two negative commandments, as it is said: 'It cannot be measured and cannot be counted.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds to רבי אלעזר. He reads the rest of the same verse and finds a second prohibition in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר used only 'לא ימד.' רב נחמן בר יצחק points out that the verse continues 'ולא יספר.' He reads each phrase as a separate לאו, so counting Jews violates two.

keyTerms.meaning: And it shall not (or cannot) be counted

steps.whatToRemember: Counting Jews directly is forbidden even for a מצוה (רבי יצחק). That is why the משנה's lottery counts fingers. The source is שאול counting with טלאים. Counting Jews violates one לאו according to רבי אלעזר, and two according to רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
He transgresses two negative commandments,
as it is said: 'It cannot be measured and cannot be counted' (Hosea 2:1).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אלעזר about how many לאוין are involved.

steps.title: Two parts of one verse seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן points out that the verse first says the Jewish people have a 'number,' and then says they cannot be counted at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said that רבי יונתן raised a contradiction. It is written: 'The number of the children of Israel will be like the sand of the sea.' It is also written: 'which cannot be measured and cannot be counted.' Which is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new problem from the same verse that רבי אלעזר and רב נחמן בר יצחק just used. One part of the verse speaks of a 'number,' and the other part says the people cannot be counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sand is enormous, but it is still a fixed amount, so 'like the sand of the sea' suggests a real, very large number. 'Cannot be counted' suggests there is no number at all. The two phrases seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'threw' two sources against each other, meaning he raised a contradiction
Like the sand of the sea

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
Rabbi Yonatan raised a contradiction:
It is written: 'And the number of the children of Israel will be'
'like the sand of the sea,'
phrases.notes: Sand is a huge amount, but it is still a set number.

phrases.english: and it is written: 'which cannot be measured and cannot be counted'?
phrases.notes: This is the same verse רבי אלעזר and רב נחמן בר יצחק just used.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the verse used for the לאוין in steps 10-11 and points out an internal contradiction within it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the verse in הושע about the number of the Jewish people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Number like sand' implies a finite count, while 'cannot be counted' implies there is no count. The two phrases appear to contradict each other.

steps.title: First answer: it depends on whether the Jewish people do ה׳'s will
steps.stepSummary: When the Jewish people do ה׳'s will, they cannot be counted. When they do not, they are like sand, which is huge but limited.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. One phrase speaks about a time when the Jewish people do ה׳'s will. The other phrase speaks about a time when they do not do ה׳'s will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each phrase describes a different time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Cannot be counted' describes the reward when the people do רצונו של מקום. 'Like the sand of the sea' describes a time when they do not, so their number is large but limited. The two phrases are not describing the same situation, so they do not contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; standard opening of an answer
The will of ה׳‎ (מָקוֹם is a name for ה׳)
Here ... there; each source refers to a different case

phrases.english: It is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם,
phrases.english: here, it speaks of a time when Israel does the will of God,
phrases.notes: This refers to 'cannot be counted.'

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: there, it speaks of a time when they do not do the will of God.
phrases.notes: This refers to 'like the sand of the sea,' a large but limited number.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בִּזְמַן שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 12 by assigning each phrase to a different spiritual situation.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן ... כאן): each phrase refers to a different time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both phrases describe the same Jewish people at the same time, so they clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doing ה׳'s will brings uncountable numbers. Not doing it brings a number like sand: huge, but limited.

steps.title: Second answer: humans cannot count them, but ה׳ can
steps.stepSummary: רבי, quoting אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי, answers that people cannot count the Jewish people, but ה׳ can.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said in the name of אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי: It is not difficult. One phrase speaks about counting by people. The other phrase speaks about counting by Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the same contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the difference is not about behavior. It is about who is doing the counting. 'Cannot be counted' means no human can count them. 'A number like sand' means ה׳ knows their exact number.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of; quoting someone else
By human hands; counting done by people
By the hands of Heaven; counting done by ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: 'רבי' here, with no name after it, means רבי יהודה הנשיא, not just any rabbi.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אָמַר מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי,
phrases.english: Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) said in the name of Abba Yosei ben Dostai:
It is not difficult: here, it means by the hand of man,
phrases.notes: People cannot count them.

phrases.english: there, it means by the hand of Heaven.
phrases.notes: ה׳ knows their number, like the grains of sand.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אָמַר מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי, לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, independent answer to the contradiction in step 12, in place of the answer in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases by who is counting (human vs. ה׳)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse says outright that there is no number, which contradicts 'number.'
steps.terutzMaskana: No person can count them, but ה׳ knows the exact number.

steps.title: A person appointed as a community leader becomes wealthy
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that once someone is appointed a leader over the community, he becomes rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נהילאי בר אידי said in the name of שמואל: Once a person is appointed as a leader over the community, he becomes wealthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching. It connects back to the verses about שאול counting the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that public leadership brings wealth with it. The proof will come from the two verses about how שאול counted the people.

keyTerms.meaning: A leader or provider over the community

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נְהִילַאי בַּר אִידִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Nehilai bar Idi said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּתְמַנָּה אָדָם פַּרְנָס עַל הַצִּיבּוּר — מִתְעַשֵּׁר.
phrases.english: Once a person is appointed leader over the community, he becomes wealthy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נְהִילַאי בַּר אִידִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, built on the two verses about שאול's counting from steps 7-9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being appointed a public leader brings wealth.

steps.title: Proof: שאול first counted with pottery, and later with sheep
steps.stepSummary: At first שאול counted the people with cheap pottery pieces (בזק). Later he counted them with sheep, which shows he had become rich.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first it is written: 'He counted them with בזק,' meaning pottery pieces. In the end it is written: 'He counted them with sheep.'
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל proves his teaching by comparing two times that שאול counted the people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here בזק is read as broken pottery pieces, which are cheap. Later שאול used sheep, which are valuable. The change from cheap to expensive counting objects shows that שאול grew wealthy after becoming king.
steps.confusionAlert: Earlier, רב אשי read בזק as the name of a place. Here שמואל reads it as pottery pieces. The same word is being read in a different way.

phrases.english: At first it is written: 'And he counted them with bezek,'
phrases.notes: בזק here means pieces of pottery, which are cheap.

phrases.english: and in the end it is written: 'And he counted them with sheep.'
phrases.notes: Sheep are valuable, which shows wealth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural proof for שמואל's teaching in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a public leader becomes wealthy
steps.raayaSupportSource: The contrast between 'ויפקדם בבזק' (שמואל א' יא) and 'ויפקדם בטלאים' (שמואל א' טו)

steps.title: Maybe the sheep belonged to the people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof: perhaps the sheep came from the people's own flocks, not from שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe the sheep were their own?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes a hole in שמואל's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each person brought his own sheep to be counted, the sheep tell us nothing about how rich שאול was. The proof would fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps; introduces an alternative possibility

phrases.english: But perhaps the sheep were from their own (flocks)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that the sheep show שאול's wealth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The sheep could have belonged to the people, so they prove nothing about שאול's own money.

steps.title: Otherwise, why would the verse bother to say it?
steps.stepSummary: If the sheep belonged to the people, there would be nothing new to learn, so the verse must be telling us about שאול's wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is special about this detail?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not mention details for no reason. If the people simply brought their own sheep, there would be no point in recording it. The detail is recorded because it shows that שאול himself could supply all those sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: The novelty or significance of the matter

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל: a public leader becomes wealthy, as seen from שאול going from pottery to sheep. The verse mentions the sheep in order to show שאול's wealth.

phrases.english: If so, what is the novelty of the matter?!
phrases.notes: The verse would have no reason to mention the sheep at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 17 and keeps the proof from step 16 standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Argument from the purpose of the verse: it would say nothing new otherwise
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sheep may have belonged to the people.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse mentions the sheep only to show שאול's own wealth.

steps.title: שאול argued with ה׳ about the valley
steps.stepSummary: רבי מני explains the words 'he fought in the valley' to mean that שאול argued with ה׳ about the matter of the valley.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he fought in the valley.' רבי מני said: it was about the matter of a valley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to another verse in the story of שאול and עמלק and explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the verse sounds like a battle in a valley. רבי מני reads it as an argument: שאול argued with ה׳ about the 'valley,' meaning the valley where the עגלה ערופה is brought. The next step explains what that argument was.

keyTerms.meaning: And he fought or argued (from רִיב, a dispute)

phrases.english: 'And he strove in the valley' (שמואל א' טו:ה):

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מָנִי: עַל עִסְקֵי נַחַל.
phrases.english: Rabbi Mani said: concerning the matter of a valley.
phrases.notes: This refers to the valley where the עגלה ערופה is brought.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having mentioned the verses about שאול, the גמרא continues explaining that same passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ויָּרב בנחל' means שאול argued about the issue of the valley of the עגלה ערופה.

steps.title: שאול's קל וחומר: if one life needs a ceremony, how much more all of עמלק
steps.stepSummary: When ה׳ told שאול to wipe out עמלק, שאול argued: the Torah requires an עגלה ערופה for a single killed person, so certainly all these lives should be spared.
steps.simpleTranslation: When ה׳ told שאול, 'Go and strike עמלק,' שאול said: If for one life the Torah said to bring an עגלה ערופה, then for all these lives, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what שאול's argument was. He used a קל וחומר to question the command.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עגלה ערופה shows how seriously the Torah treats even one unsolved killing. שאול reasoned that if one life matters that much, killing an entire nation must be far more serious. He used this to resist ה׳'s command.

keyTerms.meaning: The calf whose neck is broken, brought when a murdered body is found and the killer is unknown
All the more so; the closing formula of a קל וחומר

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows שאול using his own logic against a direct command from ה׳. That is the root of his failure with עמלק.

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְשָׁאוּל:
phrases.english: At the time when the Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Saul:
'Go and strike Amalek,'
he said: Now, if for one life
the Torah said to bring a calf whose neck is broken,
then all these lives,
all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה הָבֵא עֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'matter of the valley' that רבי מני mentioned in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאול argued with a קל וחומר from the עגלה ערופה that the lives of עמלק should be spared.

steps.title: שאול's argument about the animals and the children
steps.stepSummary: שאול adds to his argument: even if the people of עמלק sinned, the animals and the young children did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the people sinned, what did the animals do wrong? And if the adults sinned, what did the little children do wrong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting שאול's argument against ה׳'s command to destroy all of עמלק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 20, שאול reasoned from עגלה ערופה that human life is very precious. Here he adds a second point: punishment should fall only on the guilty. Animals and children did not sin, so in his view they should not be destroyed.

phrases.english: And if man has sinned,
what has the animal sinned?
And if the adults sinned,
what have the children sinned?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם אָדָם חָטָא, בְּהֵמָה מֶה חָטְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues שאול's argument from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאול argued that the innocent, meaning animals and children, should not be destroyed together with the sinners.

steps.title: A Heavenly voice: do not be overly righteous
steps.stepSummary: A בת קול rejects שאול's reasoning: 'Do not be overly righteous.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A Heavenly voice came out and said to him: 'Do not be overly righteous.'
steps.whatsHappening: Heaven answers שאול's argument and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse from קהלת tells שאול that his mercy goes too far. Showing more mercy than ה׳, who gave the command, is not true righteousness. It is disobedience dressed up as kindness.
steps.confusionAlert: The בת קול is not saying mercy is bad. It is saying that 'mercy' which goes against ה׳'s explicit command is a mistake.

phrases.english: A Heavenly voice came forth and said to him:
"Do not be overly righteous."
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers and rejects שאול's argument from steps 20–21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole of שאול's argument for sparing עמלק.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Being more merciful than ה׳'s command is false righteousness.

steps.title: A Heavenly voice: do not be overly wicked
steps.stepSummary: When שאול orders דואג to kill the כהנים of נוב, a בת קול tells him: 'Do not be overly wicked.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And when שאול said to דואג, 'Turn and strike the priests,' a Heavenly voice came out and said to him: 'Do not be overly wicked.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the opposite failure in שאול. The same man who spared עמלק later had innocent כהנים killed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two verses from קהלת form a pair. שאול was too merciful where ה׳ commanded destruction, and too cruel where there was no command at all. The second בת קול rebukes that cruelty.

keyTerms.meaning: דואג האדומי, שאול's servant who killed the כהנים

phrases.english: And at the time when Saul said to Doeg:
"Turn around and strike the priests,"
phrases.notes: שמואל א 22:18

phrases.english: a Heavenly voice came forth and said to him:
"Do not be overly wicked."
phrases.notes: קהלת 7:17

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pairs with step 22 and shows שאול's opposite mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאול was rebuked for killing the כהנים of נוב with the words 'Do not be overly wicked.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the challenge in step 27: נוב was also a sin of שאול.

steps.title: רב הונא: one with ה׳'s help need not worry
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא teaches that a person whom ה׳ helps has little to fear. שאול lost his kingdom over one sin, while דוד kept his kingdom despite two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: How little does a man whose Master helps him need to suffer or worry! שאול failed in one thing and it counted against him. דוד failed in two and it did not count against him.
steps.whatsHappening: Prompted by the story of שאול, the גמרא brings a new teaching from רב הונא. It sets up the questions that follow about which sins are meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's proof is the contrast between שאול and דוד. One sin cost שאול the throne, but two sins did not cost דוד his throne. The difference is ה׳'s support.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
How little does he suffer or worry,
a man whose Master helps him.
Saul failed with one, and it was counted against him.
David failed with two, and it was not counted against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new teaching connected to שאול's sin with עמלק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳'s support protects a person. שאול fell over one sin, while דוד survived two.

steps.title: What was שאול's one sin?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which sin רב הונא meant when he said שאול failed in one thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: שאול failed in one: what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for clarification of רב הונא's words. It is setting up its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא did not say which sin he meant. The גמרא needs to identify it before checking whether his count is accurate.

phrases.english: Saul with one: what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of רב הונא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which single sin of שאול רב הונא meant.

steps.title: The incident with אגג
steps.stepSummary: The answer: שאול's one sin was sparing אגג, king of עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The incident of אגג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the sin was the incident with אגג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול let אגג live, along with the best of the animals, against ה׳'s command. This connects directly back to the עמלק story above.

keyTerms.meaning: the incident of אגג, king of עמלק

phrases.english: The incident of Agag.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25.

steps.title: But there was also נוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the count: שאול also sinned at נוב, the city of כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the incident of נוב, the city of the priests!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that שאול had a second sin, so 'one' seems wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 already showed that שאול killed the כהנים at נוב. That looks like a second sin, which would mean שאול failed in two things just like דוד.

keyTerms.meaning: נוב, the city of the כהנים

phrases.english: But there is the incident
of Nob, the city of the priests!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיכָּא מַעֲשֶׂה דְּנוֹב עִיר הַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that שאול failed in only one sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נוב was a second sin, so the count of one appears wrong.

steps.title: שאול's fate was sealed already at אגג
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ said 'I regret that I made שאול king' right after אגג, before נוב. So one sin was enough to cost him the kingdom.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the incident of אגג it is written: 'I regret that I made שאול king.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the decision against שאול came after the אגג incident alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא was not counting every sin שאול ever did. He was counting the sins that decided his fall. ה׳ regretted making שאול king already after אגג, so the kingdom was lost over one sin, and נוב came later.

phrases.english: On the incident of Agag it is written:
"I regret that I have crowned
Saul as king."
phrases.notes: שמואל א 15:11

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Timing: the decisive verdict came before the second sin.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נוב should count as a second sin in רב הונא's statement.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one sin, אגג, caused שאול to lose the kingdom.

steps.title: What were דוד's two sins?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which two sins of דוד רב הונא meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: דוד with two: what are they?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the same clarifying question about דוד. It is setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This parallels the question about שאול in step 25. The גמרא wants to identify the two sins that did not cost דוד his kingdom.

phrases.english: David with two: what are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from שאול to the second half of רב הונא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which two sins of דוד רב הונא meant.

steps.title: אוריה and the incitement
steps.stepSummary: דוד's two sins were the killing of אוריה and the census he was incited to take.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sin of אוריה, and the sin of the incitement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names דוד's two sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד arranged for אוריה to die in battle. He was also incited to count the Jewish people, and a plague followed. Even so, he kept his kingdom.

phrases.english: That of Uriah, and that of the incitement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The killing of אוריה and the census brought about by incitement.

steps.title: But there was also בת שבע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the incident of בת שבע is a third sin of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is also the incident of בת שבע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that דוד seems to have had more than two sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking בת שבע was a separate sin from killing אוריה. So דוד appears to have three sins, not two.

phrases.english: But there is also
the incident of Bathsheba!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אִיכָּא נָמֵי מַעֲשֶׂה דְּבַת שֶׁבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The count of two sins for דוד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בת שבע would be a third sin.

steps.title: בת שבע was already punished fourfold
steps.stepSummary: דוד was already punished for בת שבע four times over: the child, אמנון, תמר, and אבשלום. So it is not counted with the other sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they already collected payment from him, as it is written: 'And he shall repay the lamb fourfold.' The child, אמנון, תמר, and אבשלום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the בת שבע sin was already paid for through punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נתן's parable of the poor man's lamb stood for בת שבע, and דוד himself ruled that the lamb must be repaid four times. That fourfold punishment came through four of his children. Since this debt was paid, it does not count among the sins that could have cost him the kingdom.

keyTerms.meaning: payment was collected from him (he was punished)
lamb, a parable for בת שבע

phrases.english: There, punishment was collected from him,
as it is written: "And the lamb
he shall repay fourfold,"
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 12:6

phrases.english: the child, Amnon, Tamar, and Avshalom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exclusion: a sin already punished is not counted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בת שבע should be counted as a third sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because דוד was already punished fourfold for בת שבע, it is excluded from the count.

steps.title: But the census was also punished, with a plague
steps.stepSummary: If sins that were already punished are not counted, the census should not count either, since it was punished with a plague.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, for the census, he was punished, as it is written: 'And ה׳ sent a plague (upon the people from the morning) until the appointed time'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the rule from step 32 against the list itself. If a punished sin doesn't count, then the census shouldn't count either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 removed בת שבע from the list because דוד was already punished for it. But the census also brought a punishment, a deadly plague. By that same logic, the census should drop off the list too, leaving דוד with only one sin.

keyTerms.meaning: They punished him for it; he already paid for it

phrases.english: There too, they punished him for it,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the census

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And the Lord sent a plague
phrases.notes: שמואל ב כד:טו

phrases.english: (upon the people from the morning) until the appointed time'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from step 32 to the census and challenges counting it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Counting the census as one of דוד's two sins.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being punished removes a sin from the count, the census was punished with a plague and should also be removed.

steps.title: The census punishment did not hit דוד's own body
steps.stepSummary: The plague struck the people, not דוד himself, so the census still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, they did not punish him in his own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refines the rule. A sin only drops off the count if דוד himself was punished in his own body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plague killed people of ישראל, but דוד personally was not struck. So the census was never 'paid for' by דוד himself and stays on the list. This adds a new condition to the rule: the punishment must be personal.

phrases.english: There, they did not punish him in his own body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 33 by narrowing the rule to personal, bodily punishment.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: punishment on the people versus punishment on דוד himself
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any punishment connected to the sin cancels it from the count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a punishment on דוד's own body cancels the sin. The census plague hit the people, so the census still counts.

steps.title: But בת שבע was also not punished on his body
steps.stepSummary: The punishments for בת שבע fell on his children, not on דוד himself, so by the new rule it should count.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, for בת שבע, they did not punish him in his own body!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the new rule from step 34 to attack the answer of step 32.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four punishments for בת שבע (the baby, אמנון, תמר, אבשלום) all happened to דוד's children. If only bodily punishment counts, then בת שבע was never paid for personally. So it should be counted as a third sin.

keyTerms.meaning: There too; the same is true in the other case

phrases.english: There too, they did not punish him in his own body!
phrases.notes: 'There' now means the בת שבע incident

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the distinction of step 34 back against step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 32 that בת שבע is not counted because it was already punished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The בת שבע punishments struck his children, not his body. Under step 34's rule, it should still count.

steps.title: דוד was personally struck with צרעת for six months
steps.stepSummary: For בת שבע, דוד himself was punished: six months of צרעת, the סנהדרין left him, and the שכינה left him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not so, they did punish him in his own body. As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: For six months דוד had צרעת, the סנהדרין separated from him, and the שכינה left him. As it is written: 'Let those who fear You return to me, and those who know Your testimonies.' And it is written: 'Restore to me the joy of Your salvation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for בת שבע there was also a personal, bodily punishment, so it really is not counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב teaches that דוד was struck with צרעת for six months, which is a punishment on his own body. The two פסוקים in תהלים prove the other parts. דוד begged 'return to me,' which shows the סנהדרין had left him. He asked 'restore to me the joy,' which shows the שכינה had left him.
steps.whatToRemember: בת שבע is not counted because דוד was punished in his own body (צרעת). The census is counted because its punishment fell on the people.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוקים are not about צרעת itself. They prove that the סנהדרין and the שכינה left him, based on his prayers asking them to 'return.'

phrases.english: No, they did punish him in his own body,
as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
For six months David was afflicted with tzara'as
and the Sanhedrin separated from him,
and the Divine Presence departed from him,
as it is written: 'Let those who fear You return to me
phrases.notes: תהלים קיט:עט, referring to the סנהדרין

phrases.english: and those who know Your testimonies.'
And it is written: 'Restore to me the joy of Your salvation.'
phrases.notes: תהלים נא:יד, referring to the שכינה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the premise of step 35 by showing a personal punishment for בת שבע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual correction backed by an אמורא's teaching and פסוקים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The בת שבע punishments fell only on דוד's children.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוד himself suffered six months of צרעת and lost the סנהדרין and the שכינה, so בת שבע is not counted.

steps.title: Another sin: accepting לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: רב said דוד accepted לשון הרע (from ציבא about מפיבשת), which would be another sin beyond two.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב say that דוד accepted לשון הרע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new possible sin of דוד that would break the count of only two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ציבא told דוד that מפיבשת was happy about דוד's downfall, and דוד believed him. According to רב, that counts as accepting לשון הרע. If so, דוד has another sin, and רב הונא's 'two sins' seems wrong.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav say:
David accepted a slanderous report!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling בת שבע, it raises a different extra sin.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that דוד had only two sins.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב says דוד accepted לשון הרע, so there is another sin on the list.

steps.title: Follow שמואל: דוד did not accept לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא agrees with שמואל, who holds that דוד did not accept לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows שמואל, who said: דוד did not accept לשון הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב הונא holds like שמואל, so there is no third sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל argue about whether דוד accepted לשון הרע. שמואל says he did not, because ציבא's report was actually true. If רב הונא follows שמואל, the list stays at two sins.

phrases.english: Like Shmuel, who said:
David did not accept a slanderous report.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 37 by placing רב הונא on the side of שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the view to one side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees דוד accepted לשון הרע.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב הונא follows שמואל, who says דוד never accepted לשון הרע.

steps.title: Even according to רב, דוד was punished: the kingdom split
steps.stepSummary: Even if דוד did accept לשון הרע, he was punished for it when the kingdom was divided between רחבעם and ירבעם, so it is not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רב, who said דוד accepted לשון הרע, he was punished for it. As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: When דוד said to מפיבשת, 'I say, you and ציבא shall divide the field,' a בת קול came out and said to him: 'רחבעם and ירבעם will divide the kingdom.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer: even with רב's view, this sin is not counted because it was already paid for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because דוד believed ציבא, he split מפיבשת's field in two. Measure for measure, a בת קול announced that his own kingdom would be split between רחבעם and ירבעם. Since he was already punished, this sin drops off the list, just like בת שבע.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's 'two sins' are the census and אוריה. The other sins are excluded: בת שבע was paid for in דוד's body, and the לשון הרע either never happened (שמואל) or was paid for with the split kingdom (רב).
steps.confusionAlert: The split kingdom came after שלמה's death, long after דוד. Still, the גמרא treats it as דוד's punishment, declared to him at the moment he divided the field.

phrases.english: And even according to Rav, who said
David accepted a slanderous report,
he was already punished for it,
as Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
At the time that David said to Mephibosheth:
'I say, you and Ziba shall divide the field,'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב יט:ל

phrases.english: a heavenly voice came out and said to him:
'Rehoboam and Jeroboam will divide the kingdom.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב נָמֵי דְּאָמַר קִבֵּל דָּוִד לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 37 that works even according to רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the 'already punished' rule from step 32
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רב, the לשון הרע must be an extra, uncounted-for sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even according to רב, דוד was punished measure for measure with the divided kingdom, so the sin is not counted.

steps.title: שאול was like a one-year-old who never tasted sin
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains 'בן שנה שאול במלכו' to mean that שאול was as innocent as a one-year-old child when he became king.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'שאול was one year old when he became king.' רב הונא said: this means he was like a one-year-old, who has never tasted the taste of sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a strange-sounding פסוק and רב הונא explains it as praise of שאול's purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול was obviously not a baby when he was crowned, so the פסוק cannot be literal. רב הונא reads it as a comparison: like a baby, שאול had no sins at all when his reign began. This supports the earlier idea that שאול had very few sins.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the פסוק literally. Nobody claims שאול was crowned as a baby. 'בן שנה' here is a comparison about his innocence.

phrases.english: "Shaul was one year old when he began to reign"
phrases.notes: I שמואל 13:1

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Like a one-year-old,
who has never tasted the taste of sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֶּן שָׁנָה שָׁאוּל בְּמׇלְכוֹ אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of דוד's sins back to שאול, describing his innocence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'בן שנה' in the פסוק mean שאול was as sinless as a one-year-old when he became king.

steps.title: Maybe one-year-old means dirty, not innocent
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק objects that 'like a one-year-old' could just as well mean covered in mud and filth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק objected: Why not say 'like a one-year-old' in the sense that a baby is dirty with mud and filth?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק challenges רב הונא's reading by offering an opposite, insulting meaning of the same comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby is innocent, but a baby is also messy. רב נחמן בר יצחק argues that the comparison does not prove praise. It could hint that שאול was spiritually 'dirty'.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak strongly objected to this:
But perhaps say "like a one-year-old"
in that he is filthy with mud and excrement?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק וְאֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading that 'בן שנה' means sinless.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison to a baby is ambiguous. It could point to dirtiness just as easily as innocence, so it is not proof of praise.

steps.title: רב נחמן's frightening dreams and his apology to שאול
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן is shown nightmares and apologizes to שאול. Only when he adds 'king of Israel' do the dreams stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: They showed רב נחמן a frightening dream. He said: 'I humbly submit to you, bones of שאול son of קיש.' He saw another frightening dream. He said: 'I humbly submit to you, bones of שאול son of קיש, king of Israel.'
steps.whatsHappening: A story shows that Heaven rejected רב נחמן's insult to שאול. He had to apologize twice, the second time with full royal honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא does not answer the objection with logic. Instead, the dreams show that the insulting reading was wrong and disrespectful. The first apology was not enough because it left out שאול's royal title. Only 'מלך ישראל' showed proper respect.

keyTerms.meaning: I humble myself before you, I beg your pardon

steps.whyThisMatters: The story teaches that one must speak of a king of Israel, and of earlier great people, with full respect, even after their death.

phrases.english: They showed Rav Nachman
a frightening dream in his sleep.
He said: I humbly submit myself to you,
O bones of Shaul son of Kish.
Again he saw a frightening dream.
He said: I humbly submit myself to you,

phrases.aramaic: עַצְמוֹת שָׁאוּל בֶּן קִישׁ מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: O bones of Shaul son of Kish, king of Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחְוִיאוּ לֵיהּ לְרַב נַחְמָן סִיּוּטָא בְּחֶלְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows through a story that the objection in step 41 was wrong.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב נחמן בר יצחק's insulting reading entirely.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The reading disrespected a righteous king. Heaven punished it, which confirms רב הונא's praise.
steps.whatToRemember: 'בן שנה' means שאול was sinless like a baby. Insulting him was punished from Heaven.

steps.title: שאול's kingdom did not last because his family had no flaw
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says שאול's dynasty did not continue because there was no blemish at all in his family background.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Why did the kingship of שאול's family not continue? Because there was no flaw in him at all.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל asks why שאול's royal line ended. He answers with a surprising reason: his family was too perfect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We would expect a flawless family to be the best choice for a lasting kingdom. שמואל says the opposite: a ruler with a 'perfect' background is missing something that keeps him humble. The next step brings the source for this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: The kingship of the house of Shaul

steps.confusionAlert: This is not criticism of שאול. The 'flaw' is about family history, and the point is that having one would have helped keep him humble.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נִמְשְׁכָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית שָׁאוּל —
phrases.english: Why did the kingship of the house of Shaul not continue?

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה בּוֹ שׁוּם דּוֹפִי,
phrases.english: Because there was no flaw in him at all,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נִמְשְׁכָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about שאול: the reason his dynasty ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאול's kingdom did not continue because his lineage had no blemish.

steps.title: A leader needs a humbling background behind him
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's rule: a community leader is appointed only if he has a 'box of creeping creatures' behind him, so he can be reminded to stay humble.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: We appoint a leader over the community only if a box of creeping creatures hangs behind him. Then, if he becomes arrogant, people can tell him: 'Look behind you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that explains שמואל's surprising reason from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'box of creeping creatures' is a picture for something embarrassing in a person's family history. If the leader becomes proud, people can remind him of his humble roots. שאול had nothing like this, so his kingdom did not last. דוד, who descended from רות the מואביה, did have such a background.

keyTerms.meaning: Leader or official of the community
A box of creeping creatures, meaning an embarrassing family background

steps.whyThisMatters: It explains the contrast with דוד, whose ancestry included תמר and רות, and whose kingdom lasted forever.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
One does not appoint a leader over the community

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן קוּפָּה שֶׁל שְׁרָצִים
phrases.english: unless a box of creeping creatures
is hanging behind him.
So that if he becomes arrogant,
they say to him: Turn and look behind you.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the principle behind שמואל's explanation.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's claim that a flawless lineage caused שאול's kingdom to end.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: a leader must have a humbling background to keep him from arrogance.

steps.title: שאול was punished for giving up his royal honor
steps.stepSummary: רב says שאול was punished because he gave up on the honor due to him as king.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Why was שאול punished? Because he gave up his honor.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching explains the root cause of שאול's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Giving up honor usually sounds like a good thing. רב says that for a king it is a failing, because a king's honor protects the nation. The next step proves this from פסוקים.
steps.confusionAlert: Humility is normally praised, but a king is not allowed to give up his honor. This is a special rule for a king, not a criticism of humility in general.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
Why was Shaul punished?
Because he gave up his honor,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב מִפְּנֵי מָה נֶעֱנַשׁ שָׁאוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further teaching about שאול, now about the cause of his punishment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שאול was punished because, as king, he gave up the honor due to him.

steps.title: Proof from the verses: שאול stayed silent and נחש attacked
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים show that שאול ignored those who disrespected him, and right afterward נחש העמוני attacked יבש גלעד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And worthless men said, How can this one save us? They despised him and brought him no gift, and he acted as if he did not hear.' And it is written right after: 'And נחש העמוני came up and camped against יבש גלעד.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two neighboring פסוקים to prove רב's claim that שאול gave up his honor and that this caused trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק shows שאול keeping quiet when people insulted him. The very next פסוק describes an enemy attack. Putting them side by side teaches that his weak response invited the attack. A king who does not defend his honor looks weak to enemies.

keyTerms.meaning: As if he were silent, pretending not to hear

steps.whatToRemember: שאול was praised as sinless, his dynasty ended because his family was too flawless to keep him humble, and he was punished for giving up a king's honor, which led to נחש's attack.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "And base fellows said:
phrases.notes: I שמואל 10:27

phrases.english: How can this one save us?
And they despised him and brought him no gift,
and he was as one who kept silent."
And it is written: "And Nachash the Ammonite came up
phrases.notes: I שמואל 11:1, the very next verse

phrases.english: and camped against Yavesh Gilad, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves רב's statement from the order of the פסוקים.
steps.raayaObject: רב's claim that שאול gave up his honor and was punished for it.
steps.raayaSupportSource: I שמואל 10:27, where שאול stays silent when insulted, followed immediately by I שמואל 11:1, where נחש העמוני attacks.

steps.title: Opening of a new teaching about every Torah scholar
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, begins a teaching about how any תלמיד חכם should act. The teaching itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: Any Torah scholar...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new statement. It names who said it and starts with 'any תלמיד חכם.' The actual rule comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְאָמַר' ('and he said') shows this is another teaching from the same רבי יוחנן quoted in step 44. It follows straight after the lesson that שאול was punished for giving up his honor. So expect a rule about how a תלמיד חכם must protect the respect owed to him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he said'. Introduces another statement from the same sage.
'In the name of'. The speaker is passing on a teaching from an earlier sage.
'Any Torah scholar'. The statement is about every scholar, not one specific case.

steps.confusionAlert: This passage stops in the middle of a sentence. Do not treat 'any Torah scholar' as a full teaching. The rule about what a תלמיד חכם must do comes in the next part of the text.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
phrases.notes: The 'and' ties this to the earlier teaching of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: Any Torah scholar
phrases.notes: A new rule starts here, and the sentence finishes on the next amud.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (if read as further support for רב's point about שאול)
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of steps 45-46, where שאול was punished for giving up his honor. It moves from a king to every תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated on this amud. The opening sets up a general rule about how any תלמיד חכם should handle his honor.
